text:
Hana Kim: FYI a community contributor raised a parity failure for our Remix edge starter used in the eval harness. It only shows up on the edge runtime (Cloudflare/Netlify Edge) where fetch streaming + auth refresh interplay is different. Repro steps below.

Hana Kim: Repro: clone examples/remix-edge-starter, yarn && yarn dev (node/middleware), set REDWOOD_API_KEY, then run the eval harness in edge emulation mode (we use @vercel/edge-runtime). After a short wait the /api/stream endpoint returns partial stream then 401 mid-stream and the harness marks it as regression.

Vikram Rao: I can repro locally using wrangler dev. Logs show: "fetch: 401 unauthorized during response body read". Browser client gets truncated SSE and abort.

Lina Torres: snippet from app/routes/api/stream.tsx:```ts
export const loader = async ({ request }) => {
  const stream = await redwood.chat.stream({ messages });
  return new Response(stream, { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' } });
};
```

Owen Park: Edge runtimes don't allow shared global state easily. Our JS SDK uses a global in-memory refresh lock which works in Node but not in multi-isolate edge envs. So when token expires mid-stream a different isolate won't see the refresh and aborts.

Hana Kim: proposed approaches: 1) make stream client fail-fast and surface a specific error so harness can retry at application level; 2) add a short-lived signed token glue (signed ephemeral token issued by control plane) so the edge instance uses a self-contained credential that remains valid for the request duration; 3) fall back to polling generation for edge starters in examples.

Vikram Rao: Short-term: update the example to set REDWOOD_SDK_ASSUME_RETRY=true and restart the stream once on 401 (idempotent endpoints only). Long-term: we should offer an ephemeral token flow that the starter can demonstrate (fetch /api/ephemeral -> get token valid for 30s). That avoids global refresh state.

Lina Torres: I sketched an ephemeral-token flow in the repo: /api/ephemeral issues signed token via server-side KMS call (mocked in examples). The edge client then calls the streaming endpoint with that signed token in Authorization header. It survives mid-stream because the token has shorter lifetime but is bound to a single request.

Owen Park: security + perf note: issuing ephemeral tokens for every request increases control plane ops, but for a starter demo it's fine. We'll mark it as "example-only" and not recommend at scale.

devex-bot: CI issue created: https://ci.internal.redwood/gh/examples/remix-edge-starter/11 -> tests/eval/streaming-edge -> 2423456820

Hana Kim: opened PR with two commits: 1) fallback restart-once in example client with clear README caveats; 2) ephemeral-token example in /examples/ephemeral-token with a mock KMS flow and harness fixture. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/123

Vikram Rao: added a unit test in sdk-edge-shim that throws when global refresh is accessed in edge mode; added runtime check that warns during init. Will follow up to make the SDK detect edge-like environment and expose recommended pattern in docs.

Lina Torres: updated example README and eval harness fixture to run the ephemeral flow in edge emulation CI job. Also added a note about streaming caveats and how to force token expiry locally for debugging: REDWOOD_TEST_EXPIRE_MS=1000.

Owen Park: merging the example PR after test updates. We'll keep evaluating if we should adapt runtime to use SharedArrayBuffer & cross-isolate hooks for supported platforms, but not in the near-term.

Hana Kim: thanks all. marking this as resolved for the parity harness once examples CI green. If anyone sees similar in other starters, please drop repro here. :sparkles:
